hints: Use polynomial or synthetic division by x+1, including zero coefficients for x³ and x terms.
Stop at a constant remainder and verify divisor×quotient+remainder reconstructs 3x⁴−2x².
walkthrough:
Write the dividend including zero placeholders for missing degree terms:
$$P(x) = 3x^4 + 0x^3 - 2x^2 + 0x + 0$$
$$\text{Divisor: } x + 1$$

Perform polynomial division step-by-step:
$$\text{Step 1: } \dfrac{3x^4}{x} = 3x^3 \implies (3x^4 + 0x^3) - 3x^3(x + 1) = -3x^3$$
$$\text{Step 2: } \text{Bring down } -2x^2: \quad \dfrac{-3x^3}{x} = -3x^2 \implies (-3x^3 - 2x^2) - (-3x^2)(x + 1) = x^2$$
$$\text{Step 3: } \text{Bring down } 0x: \quad \dfrac{x^2}{x} = x \implies (x^2 + 0x) - x(x + 1) = -x$$
$$\text{Step 4: } \text{Bring down } 0: \quad \dfrac{-x}{x} = -1 \implies (-x + 0) - (-1)(x + 1) = 1$$

Assemble the full quotient and constant remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = 3x^3 - 3x^2 + x - 1$$
$$\text{Remainder} = 1$$
$$3x^4 - 2x^2 = (x + 1)\left(3x^3 - 3x^2 + x - 1\right) + 1$$

ai_rubric.Polynomial Division and Remainder Condit: Divides and reaches a partial quotient of the form $3x^3\pm3x^2$, or write $3x^4-2x^2=(x+1)(Ax^3+Bx^2+Cx+D)+Ex+F$ and reaches $A=3$, $B=\pm3$. Concludes with Quotient $3x^3-3x^2+x-1$. Remainder $1$. Polynomial division gives quotient $3x^3-3x^2+x-1$; remainder $1$.
